resources.string: Plug your phone into your TV with a USB-C cable and tap Refresh.
Connected in USB host mode. VID 0x%1$s, PID 0x%2$s — this is likely your TV.
A USB device is connected, but it could not be clearly identified as a TV. See the technical details below.
Connected via the Android Open Accessory (AOA) protocol.
Connected to a USB host (phone is the USB device)
Your phone is in device/peripheral mode, so it cannot read the host\'s (TV\'s) name. See the setup notes for the configuration that lets the phone identify the TV.
Sends one tap to the TV through the relay on your laptop (tools/relay.py). USB detection above is unaffected.
Not sent yet. Start tools/relay.py on your laptop, then tap Send Test Tap.
The phone itself is the adb client. No laptop, no relay - the phone and TV only need to be on the same Wi-Fi (e.g. the phone\'s own hotspot).
Not connected. Enable USB debugging (+ network debugging) on the TV, enter the TV\'s IP, then tap Connect.
Connected to %1$s:%2$d - authorized. Tap Send Test Tap.
Tap sent to %1$d,%2$d (empty output = success). Watch the TV.
Tap failed - connection lost (%1$s). Tap Connect again.
Tap command timed out - the TV may have disconnected. Tap Connect again.
Not connected to the TV. Tap Connect first.
Enter the TV\'s IP address first.
TV not reachable at %1$s:%2$d. Check: same Wi-Fi/hotspot, correct IP, and USB debugging + network debugging enabled on the TV.
Reached the TV, but it did not authorize this phone in time. Check the TV screen for the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt, accept it, then tap Connect again.
The TV closed the connection before authorizing this phone. Check the TV screen for the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt, accept it, then tap Connect again.
Could not generate or load the adb RSA key pair.
